messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated artifact fetch failures for huggingface model artifacts (vicuna-13b / repo: redwood/vicuna-13b). 429s and timeouts from hf.co reported by fetcher pool. Error rate spiked ~08:12 UTC. Auto-escalating to incidents. Link: https://status.huggingface.co/ (investigating)

devon: I'm seeing the same from fetcher logs — lots of 429 + some connection timeouts. Cold-starts are failing to pull weights. example log:
```
2026-03-15T08:11:52Z fetcher ERROR huggingface fetch failed: 429 Too Many Requests (X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0)
2026-03-15T08:12:04Z runtime WARN model load aborted: artifact download failed
```

alex: paging @devon (oncall). @maria @ryan FYI. Raising to P1 until we understand customer impact. I'll coordinate comms.

maria: jumping in. checking recent deployments to rule out config change. nothing obvious in deploys. reproducing locally against hf api now.

ryan: question — are we seeing auth 401s or purely rate limiting? could be HF global rate-limiter for our token.

devon: all 429s, headers show low remaining quota. No 401s. This looks like HF-side throttling on artifact downloads. Also seeing `X-RateLimit-Reset` header in some responses.

julia: immediate mitigation ideas:
- short-term: route cold-start fetches to a smaller cached model (7B) for new requests
- medium-term: enable local artifact cache (S3-backed) to serve artifact blobs when HF is rate-limiting
- add client-side exponential backoff + jitter and a circuit breaker to avoid hammering HF and to fail fast to fallback

infra-sre: agree. Can deploy a quick patch to fetcher to use `--prefer-cache` and fall back to local S3 mirror. I can push a hotfix to the service that orchestrates artifact pulls. minimal change:
```
# in fetcher config
artifact_sources:
  - s3://redwood-artifact-mirror/
  - https://huggingface.co/
```

customer-success: two enterprise customers raised tickets that models failed to load ~08:15 UTC. They reported errors in prod when scaling up new workers. They want an ETA.

alex: @customer-success pls gather affected customer ids + contact preference. I'll draft a short status note once we have confirmation of impact.

devon: tested direct curl to HF artifact endpoint, getting 429 with reset header. snippet:
```
curl -i "https://huggingface.co/api/models/redwood/vicuna-13b" -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678891200
```

oncall-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV-2 (service degradation). Created ticket INF-3247 and linked to PagerDuty incident PD-4421. Assigned oncall: @devon for immediate response and @ryan for handoff at 09:00 UTC.

maria: deploying config patch to prefer S3 mirror now (canary 10% traffic). Will monitor fetch success metrics.

infra-sre: added temporary client-side circuit breaker in config to stop fetch retries after 3 consecutive 429s for a given model for 5m, then fallback to smaller model. Patch pushed to fetcher, rollout in progress.

julia: code snippet for exponential backoff (node fetcher):
```
async function fetchWithBackoff(url){
  for(let i=0;i<5;i++){
    try { return await fetch(url); }
    catch(e){ await sleep(100*Math.pow(2,i) + jitter()); }
  }
  throw new Error('fetch failed after retries');
}
```

devon: after canary, S3 mirror fetches succeeded for canary instances. Cold-start failure rate dropped from ~28% to ~6% in the canary group.

alex: good signal. Rolling to 50% while we wait for HF recovery. @customer-success please let impacted customers know we have a mitigation and are rolling a patch; estimated full mitigation within ~30-45m depending on HF rate-limit relief.

customer-success: acknowledged. I'll send an interim note: "We detected 3rd-party artifact hosting rate limits affecting some model cold-starts. We've enabled a temporary mirror and fallback; engineers are monitoring. We'll update once HF issue resolves." Will include affected customer ids.

devon: note — we should also enable lightweight re-routing: if artifact fetcher sees header `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` then switch subsequent fetches to mirror automatically without waiting for retries.

infra-sre: added rule in fetcher: immediate fallback to mirror on 429 with zero remaining. Also logging which customer/route experienced fallback for downstream billing/observability.

alex: any contact established with Hugging Face support/status team?

devon: I opened a ticket with HF support (case 2026-03-15-77). They responded acknowledging higher-than-normal artifact traffic; they said they're investigating token-scoped rate limits and will follow up with an ETA.

julia: ops follow-ups for postmortem:
- ensure mirror sync job runs more frequently for top 20 production models
- add tenant-scoped artifact quotas and pre-warm hooks for scheduled scaling events
- add an observability dashboard for artifact fetch 429s + circuit breaker triggers

ryan: taking follow-up ownership after 09:00 UTC. I will run through checklist and coordinate with infra-sre for durable mirror and add an automated pre-warm pipeline for scheduled autoscale.

devon: handing off — I've documented steps in the PD incident, left current logs and commands. Key things to watch:
- artifact_fetch_429_rate (should be <1% after mirror rollout)
- cold_start_failure_rate
- customers reporting new errors

oncall-bot: Handoff notification posted. Next oncall: @ryan. Follow-up ticket: OPS-879 (mirror durability + pre-warm automation).

alex: status update for slack/stakeholders: "We experienced 3rd-party rate-limits from Hugging Face causing some new model cold-starts to fail. Mitigation: enabled S3 mirror + client-side circuit breaker + smaller-model fallback. Impact reduced significantly; engineering is monitoring. HF investigating root cause." Posting to #general in 10m.

customer-success: sent interim note to affected customers. One customer asked for a timeline for a permanent fix; we offered pre-warm mirror + SLA discussion.

devon: around 08:46 UTC HF reports partial recovery; I see 200s from HF for some artifact endpoints now. Starting to observe fetches from HF succeed again in canary.

maria: rolling mirror preference back to allow HF to serve again while keeping mirror as fallback. Watching error rates.

infra-sre: created follow-up infra task to increase mirror sync frequency and add a signed URL cache layer for large artifacts. Assigned to infra-sre team.

oncall-bot: Incident status: Mitigated. Switching to monitoring. Please keep thread open for postmortem notes and add any residual customer impact.

alex: thanks team — excellent fast mitigation. Devon, Ryan — please collaborate on the postmortem doc and include timeline + HF ticket reference. I'll coordinate customer comms tomorrow morning.

devon: documenting timeline now and will start a rough postmortem draft in docops. Adding HF case id and logs.

ryan: taking ownership for follow-ups. Leaving handoff note in Ops board.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active response at 09:40 UTC. Final impact estimate: ~12% of cold-starts for vicuna-13b affected during the 08:11-08:46 UTC window; 4 customers reported degraded behavior; no data loss; mitigation applied by 08:37 UTC (mirror+fallback).
